title: Advance Beneficiary Notices
text: Physicians must provide advance notices before they provide services that they know or believe Medicare does not consider medically necessary or that Medicare will not reimburse. Beneficiaries who are not notified before they receive such services are not responsible for payment. As a result, the OIG intends to examine the use of advance notices to Medicare beneficiaries and their financial impact on beneficiaries and providers.
source_document: Massachusetts Medical Society, Fraud and Abuse Compliance: Implementing a Compliance Plan (2003) (KB 2/USA/MAfraud.PDF)

title: Physician Evaluation and Management Codes
text: The OIG will continue its initiative to determine whether physicians correctly coded E&M services in physician offices and effectively used documentation guidelines.
source_document: Massachusetts Medical Society, Fraud and Abuse Compliance: Implementing a Compliance Plan (2003) (KB 2/USA/MAfraud.PDF)

title: Consultations
text: The OIG will determine the appropriateness of billings for physician consultation services.
source_document: Massachusetts Medical Society, Fraud and Abuse Compliance: Implementing a Compliance Plan (2003) (KB 2/USA/MAfraud.PDF)

title: Services and Supplies Incident to Physicians' Services
text: Physicians may bill for the services provided by allied health professionals such as nurses, technicians, and therapists as incident to their professional services. Incident-to services, which are paid at 100 percent of the Medicare physician fee schedule, must be provided by an employee of the physician and under the physician's direct supervision. The OIG will investigate the quality and appropriateness of these billings.

title: Reassignment of Benefits
text: The OIG will examine the use of staffing companies and how this practice affects emergency department physicians to identify any vulnerabilities in relation to Medicare reassignment rules.
source_document: Massachusetts Medical Society, Fraud and Abuse Compliance: Implementing a Compliance Plan (2003) (KB 2/USA/MAfraud.PDF)

title: Physicians at Teaching Hospitals
text: The OIG is continuing its initiative to verify compliance with Medicare rules governing payment for physician services provided in the teaching hospital setting to ensure that claims accurately reflect the level of service provided to patients.
source_document: Massachusetts Medical Society, Fraud and Abuse Compliance: Implementing a Compliance Plan (2003) (KB 2/USA/MAfraud.PDF)

title: Billing for Residents' Services
text: Medicare regulations allow residents, who are licensed physicians, to be issued physician identification numbers for purposes of billing Medicare for their services. Residents may bill Medicare only when they are “moonlighting,” which is defined as providing medical treatment, other than in their field of study, in an outpatient clinic or an emergency room. The OIG will determine whether hospitals have improperly used residents' physician identification numbers to bill Medicare.
